note: Per-case tolerance for the cross-language comparison, in units in the last place.
The default is 0: R and Python must agree bit for bit.
A non-zero entry is allowed only where the response family applies a transcendental to the
linear predictor. IEEE-754 requires correct rounding for +, -, *, / and sqrt, but not for
exp() or log(), and R for Windows (MinGW-w64) and CPython (UCRT) do not share a libm.
control_rt_as_gaussian.json is the control that pins this down: it is crossed_mixed_rt with
the family switched to gaussian, so it consumes an identical RNG stream and an identical
linear predictor. It agrees bit for bit, which leaves exp() as the only possible source of
the residual difference in the shifted_lognormal original.
Measured over 200,000 draws in the log-RT range, R and CPython exp() disagree on 0.44% of
arguments by up to 6 ulp, and log() on 0.12% by up to 1 ulp. The 8-ulp allowance leaves
headroom for a third platform's libm while staying far below any statistically meaningful
difference (~1.8e-15 relative). A logic error would show as a much larger gap, as a
differing row count, or as a differing non-numeric cell, all of which still fail.
stress_exgaussian is currently exact on this platform, but its value path applies log() to a
uniform draw, so it belongs to the same class as the two lognormal cases and is classified
with them rather than on the accident of one seed agreeing.
